case_metadata.drug_detail: 0.25 mg subcutaneous once weekly, titrated per labeling
case_metadata.policy_pathway: Section 2 — General coverage criteria, A. Initial Authorization
plan_variant_evidence: Denial letter plan line: 'Commercial employer group pharmacy benefit (fully insured, Ohio)'
Denial letter cites Section 2, not Section 3
case_metadata.design_note: The note never uses the words 'lifestyle modification', 'dietitian', 'programme enrolment' or 'exercise prescription'. It describes a church-hall walking group and an employer wellbeing challenge — which are exactly what the policy means by 'community-based program' and 'behavioral support'. The payer looked for clinical-sounding referrals and found none. The criterion is satisfied in substance and unmatched in vocabulary.

denial_ground_truth.denial_reason_text: The submitted records do not document lifestyle modification; no dietitian referral, programme enrolment or documented dietary or exercise prescription was identified.
denial_ground_truth.cited_policy_reference: UnitedHealthcare Pharmacy, Clinical Pharmacy Programs — Prior Authorization/Notification - Plans with Weight Loss/Appetite Suppression Medication Coverage (Program Number 2026 P 1114-20, effective 5/1/2026), Section 2, Coverage Criteria, A. Initial Authorization
denial_ground_truth.cited_requirement_text: Used as an adjunct to lifestyle modification (e.g., dietary or caloric restriction, exercise, behavioral support, community-based program)
denial_ground_truth.denial_accuracy_note: The denial quotes the criterion in full, including the four examples. Its error is that it then applied a narrower test — clinical referral or formal programme enrolment — than the criterion states, and missed the community-based and behavioral-support activity the record describes.

policy_ground_truth.policy_name: Prior Authorization/Notification - Plans with Weight Loss/Appetite Suppression Medication Coverage

criteria.requirement: Used as an adjunct to lifestyle modification, which the policy illustrates as dietary or caloric restriction, exercise, behavioral support, or a community-based program. No minimum duration, no supervision requirement and no referral requirement is stated.
criteria.policy_reference: Section 2, Coverage Criteria, A. Initial Authorization, 1.c
criteria.policy_support_text: Used as an adjunct to lifestyle modification (e.g., dietary or caloric restriction, exercise, behavioral support, community-based program)

criteria.requirement: Body Mass Index of 30 kg/m2 or greater.
criteria.policy_reference: Section 2, Coverage Criteria, A. Initial Authorization, 1.d(1)
criteria.policy_support_text: Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 30 kg/m2 or for pediatric patients a BMI > 95th percentile

criteria.requirement: Treatment is being requested for appetite suppression or weight loss.
criteria.policy_reference: Section 2, Coverage Criteria, A. Initial Authorization, 1.a(1)
criteria.policy_support_text: Treatment is being requested for appetite suppression or weight loss

criteria.requirement: Patient is 12 years of age or older for Wegovy injection.
criteria.policy_reference: Section 2, Coverage Criteria, A. Initial Authorization, 1.b(1)
criteria.policy_support_text: Patient is ≥ 12 years of age (for Qsymia, Saxenda, Wegovy injection and Xenical)

scope_notes: The criterion's examples are introduced by 'e.g.' and are illustrative rather than exhaustive. A community-based program and behavioral support are two of the four named illustrations, so activity of that kind is squarely within the criterion rather than an extension of it.
This policy sets no minimum duration for lifestyle modification and does not require it to be clinically supervised or clinician-referred. Reading in such a requirement is the error made in case 003.

evidence_ground_truth.evidence_timing_note: The 2026-07-06 note was submitted and reviewed. The qualifying activity is described in the note's own vocabulary rather than the policy's.

expected_evidence.evidence_text: A weekly three-mile walking group run from her church hall attended since April with one missed week, which is exercise and a community-based program; the employer's six-week 'Better Plates' challenge over May and June with weekly group sessions on portion size, label reading and batch cooking plus a food diary, which is behavioral support and a community-based program; and specific dietary changes — two cans of regular cola stopped, packed lunches four days in five, weekend batch cooking. Plan item 1 states the medication is to be added to what she is already doing, not to replace it, and names each element she will continue.
expected_evidence.evidence_location: SUBJECTIVE, paragraphs two and three; PLAN item 1

expected_evidence.evidence_text: Height 5 ft 2 in, weight 191 lb, BMI 34.9 kg/m2; 195 lb, BMI 35.7, on 04/13/2026.
Assessment item 1 is obesity; the plan requests semaglutide for weight.
DOB 03/07/1968; age 58 at the time of the request.

missing_evidence.description: No dietitian referral, no formal weight-management programme enrolment through the health system, and no written exercise prescription. None of these is required by the criterion.

per_criterion.reason: The record documents exercise, behavioral support and a community-based program — three of the four illustrations the criterion gives — together with specific dietary restriction, and the plan states the drug is an adjunct to them.
The request is for weight loss.

supported_claims: The policy's own examples of lifestyle modification include a community-based program and behavioral support, both of which the record documents.
The member has attended a weekly walking group since April and completed a six-week employer nutrition programme with a food diary she has maintained.
The plan of care states the medication is to be added to those measures rather than replace them.
The policy does not require a clinician referral, a formal programme enrolment, or any minimum duration.
unsupported_claims: That the member was referred to a dietitian or enrolled in a medically supervised programme.
That the member completed a three-month or six-month structured programme as a policy requirement.
That the member's prediabetes or hypertension is needed to establish eligibility at this BMI.

facts_allowed_in_appeal: The member has attended a weekly three-mile walking group run from her church hall since April 2026, missing one week.
The member completed the employer's six-week 'Better Plates' challenge across May and June 2026, with weekly group sessions on portion size, label reading and batch cooking, and a food diary.
The member has maintained the food diary since the programme ended.
The member stopped two cans of regular cola a day, takes a packed lunch four days in five, and batch cooks at weekends.
Documented BMI on July 6, 2026 was 34.9 kg/m2, with height 5 feet 2 inches and weight 191 pounds.
The plan of care states the medication is to be added to those measures rather than to replace them.
The member was 58 years of age at the time of the request.
facts_not_allowed_in_appeal: The member was referred to a dietitian.
The member enrolled in a medically supervised weight management programme.
The member completed six months of lifestyle modification.
UnitedHealthcare's program requires a minimum duration of lifestyle modification.
The member failed a trial of phentermine, Qsymia, Contrave, or orlistat.
The member has lost 5 percent of baseline body weight.
